results.name: Seated Plate Front Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a weight plate at its sides in front of your thighs.
Raise the plate in front of you to shoulder height with straight arms.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't lean back.
Use a light plate.
results.description: Seated Plate Front Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Seated Plate Side Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a light plate in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows.
Don't shrug.
results.description: Seated Plate Side Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

results.name: Seated Shoulder Flexor Depressor Retractor Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your back straight.
Extend both arms down to your sides, then lean back slightly.
Bring both arms about a foot behind you, keeping them straight, and place your hands on the floor with your fingers pointing forward.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your shoulders. Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Ensure your arms remain straight and your hands are firmly placed on the floor to maximize the stretch in your shoulders.
Avoid lifting your shoulders towards your ears; keep them relaxed and down to deepen the stretch.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and prevent slipping.
results.description: Seated Shoulder Flexor Depressor Retractor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Seated Shoulder Press Barbell
instructions: Sit on a bench with a backrest, feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Rest the barbell on your upper chest.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your elbows, keeping your back firmly against the backrest.
Fully extend your arms at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell is directly above your head.
Lower the barbell back down to your upper chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms to avoid strain.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to protect your joints.
Exhale as you press the barbell up and inhale as you lower it down.
results.description: Seated Shoulder Press Barbell is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Shoulder Abduction
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Slowly raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, forming a T shape with your body. Keep your palms facing down and your elbows slightly bent.
Hold the position for a moment, feeling the activation in your shoulders.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move your arms slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise your arms and inhaling as you lower them.
Ensure your shoulders stay relaxed and away from your ears throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum to lift your arms; focus on using your shoulder muscles.
results.description: Shoulder Abduction is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Shoulder Circle
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed, hanging straight down by your sides.
Begin by making small circular motions with your shoulders, moving them backward in a controlled manner.
Gradually increase the size of the circles, maintaining a steady pace.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move your shoulders slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you complete each circle and inhaling as you start the next.
Avoid using momentum to move your shoulders; focus on using your shoulder muscles.
results.description: Shoulder Circle is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Shoulder Extension
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms straight by your sides.
Slowly extend your arms straight forward, and up overhead, keeping them straight and parallel to each other .
Hold the top position for a moment. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise your arms overhead and inhaling as you lower them back down.
Ensure your shoulders stay relaxed and away from your ears throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum to lift your arms; focus on using your shoulder muscles.
results.description: Shoulder Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Side Lateral Raise Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the middle of a resistance band under both feet. Hold one handle in each hand, arms down by your sides, and palms facing inward.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a "T" shape with your body. Focusing on lifting with your shoulders and keeping your palms facing down.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the band.
results.description: Side Lateral Raise Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Position an adjustable bench under the Smith machine and set it to a vertical position. Adjust the barbell to your shoulder height.
Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and press it upward until your arms are fully extended above your head.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your back remains flat against the bench throughout the movement.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to press the weight, avoiding excessive strain on your neck.
Keep your elbows slightly bent at the top to avoid straining your elbow joints.
results.description: Smith Machine Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Standing Arnold Press Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Your palms should be facing backward, and your elbows should be bent.
Begin to press the dumbbells overhead. As you press, rotate your palms so they face forward at the top of the movement.
Fully extend your arms at the top, ensuring your biceps are near your ears.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position by rotating your palms back towards your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Rotate your wrists smoothly during the pressing and lowering phases to avoid strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the weights up and inhaling as you lower them back down.
Focus on the full range of motion to engage all parts of the shoulder muscles effectively.
results.description: Standing Arnold Press Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps.
